classification: implementation deviation from the frozen spec, caught on inspection of the output
the_deviation: D2_SPEC_FROZEN.json specified the evaluation set as INNER_VAL's own_flag_stolen subset, sized at ~1,147 decision points across 17 seeds -- a PLAIN-row count. d2_evaluate_recovery.py instead restricted to BRANCH rows, yielding only 16 states.
why_the_metric_does_not_require_branch_r: d_B(o) = V_hat(o, pi_B, B) - V_hat(o, pi_A, B) queries BOTH frozen teachers at the same observation o. It needs an observation and a pole, not a stored counterfactual pair. Restricting to branch rows was an unnecessary constraint that shrank the evaluation set roughly 70-fold.

why_attempt_1_is_unusable.1_wrong_set: 16 states is not the frozen evaluation set
why_attempt_1_is_unusable.2_verdict_logic_misfired_on_tiny_n: the recorded verdict was REPRESENTATION_CAPACITY_LIMITED, reached via the 'rung3 ucb95 < 0.5' branch. With n=16 the bootstrap CIs were [0.000, 0.357], [0.000, 0.429], [0.000, 0.471] -- all three rungs overlapping almost entirely and all including zero. That branch fired because the sample was too small to exclude 0.5, NOT because there was evidence of a capacity limit. On this data the honest reading is INCONCLUSIVE.

superseded_numbers_preserved.metric: d_B(o) = V_hat(o,pi_B,B) - V_hat(o,pi_A,B), teacher-vs-teacher, Gate 0B convention
superseded_numbers_preserved.eval_set: INNER_VAL own_flag_stolen pole-B subset -- reused development-side diagnostic resource, NOT held-out confirmation, NOT a gate

correction: re-run on the frozen spec's plain-state evaluation set; verdict thresholds NOT changed
verdict_thresholds_unchanged: the monotonicity and margin rules from D2_SPEC_AMENDMENT_1 are left exactly as frozen. Only the evaluation SET is corrected to match the spec. Changing the thresholds after seeing a result would be the prohibited move.
